items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: there was three of them that were inspired by Freddie James... and then there was Billy Yates and Baby Lawrence.

ctx.x: I just said to you, Chuck, that that looked to me like cramps and paddling rolls and things. Was that a little bit before the paddling roll really became the paddling roll and the cramp? So, let me see, now, I would say that Freddie James probably inspired whoever it was, and that would be interesting to know who did, who was the first person who did bring about the paddling roll and the cramp? Because you say that wasn't quite the paddling roll and it wasn't quite a cramp. So it's obviously whoever were the…

Yeah. Well, there were three of them that were inspired by Freddie James, but the original paddling roll came from a tap dancer known as Billy Adams and Ground Hog, see, and then there was Billy Yates and Baby Lawrence.
He was the modernistic debonair, what you would call. I called him the youngest pioneer that came into being of tap dancing, and --
